page: Microsoft Azure E32-16as_v5 is an EASv5-series memory-optimized virtual machine hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 256 GB of RAM, establishing a high ratio of 16 GB per virtual CPU. The instance provides no bundled local disk storage and contains no discrete GPUs, necessitating external network-attached volumes for persistent data storage.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-thread execution, highlighted by top-quartile results in stress-ng single-core tests and small-scale language model text generation. Multi-threaded CPU execution and PassMark metrics align with the median across comparable instances, reflecting steady computational throughput for 16 vCPUs. Memory subsystems demonstrate high cached read throughput exceeding 1000 GB/sec, though uncached large-block write bandwidth measures lower at 22.78 GB/sec.

The constrained vCPU allocation relative to the 256 GB memory footprint delivers qualitative cost advantages for software stacks licensed per core that still mandate substantial memory buffers. However, the absence of local NVMe storage introduces network-dependent latency for write-intensive disk operations. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, medium-scale ETL batching, and analytics platforms requiring extensive RAM without needing high parallel core counts.
description: Microsoft Azure E32-16as_v5 is a memory-optimized cloud instance within the EASv5 family running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical AMD EPYC 7763 cores operating at 3.525 GHz, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache. It provides 256 GB of RAM, resulting in an elevated ratio of 16 GB of memory per vCPU. Hardware accelerators and local disk storage are absent, requiring workloads to rely on remote storage solutions. In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates strong single-core compute performance and high throughput for small-model text generation, while uncached write memory bandwidth registers in the lower quartile. With its constrained core count relative to total RAM capacity, the instance offers licensing and compute cost efficiencies for memory-bound architectures. The E32-16as_v5 fits memory-intensive applications including Redis deployments, in-memory relational databases, and enterprise data caching frameworks.
